But with him I am happy for the first time in my life.
Marina, help me, my foot hurts!
Be a real man at last and go home.

meanings.en: to be ill, to be sick

examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: On the earliest occasion. Core Russian adv meaning 'for the first time' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я впервые в жизни вижу такое.

examples.text: Но с ним я впервые в жизни счастлива.
examples.trans: But with him I am happy for the first time in my life.
The chef praised the young cook for the first time.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.
Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

meanings.note: Contrast дома = at home. Core Russian adv meaning '(to) home, homeward' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.

examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: In a genuine and real manner. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-настоящему').

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'длец'). Common masculine noun meaning 'scoundrel, villain, cad' in everyday Russian.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.note: Всё получилось = it all worked out. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.
